notes.page_account: The page continues the claim that a homotopy type can be reconstructed through its fundamental infinity-groupoid and that the system of n-categories includes all cohomological operations. It then proposes a similarly complete correspondence for homotopy types associated with stratifications, via categories of n-champs locally constant on the strata, and an expected recovery of a mixed homotopy type from a subcategory of an abelian derived category together with derived operations. These are source assertions and expectations, not conclusions established by this transcription.

notes.page_date_title_evidence: Author page 39 is dark manuscript ink at top center. Archive pencil 184 is at bottom left. No date, heading, closing or signature appears on this sheet. The metadata value their_page=183 was not substituted for the observed author number.
notes.paragraph_evidence: L9 is visibly indented after the preceding parenthetical block and cancelled Mais. L17 begins at the ordinary left margin after L16 fills the line, without an exceptional blank or separator, and remains within the same paragraph.
notes.math_triggered_reading_decisions: The small infinity sign, (n+1)- replacement, derived L and R and underline scope were inspected as consequential notation. No mathematical expectation was used to invent a missing letter, erase old ink or normalize an ending. The n versus n+1 relationship was only transcribed, not independently established.
notes.proof_status: No proof or mathematical verification was attempted. check_events is intentionally empty; tracing glyphs, resolving indices, following the prose and recognizing operator notation are visual transcription, not proof checks.
H_editorial_claims: Archive 184 and author page 39 are confirmed visually.
The et overwrite is present, but H's text omits the visible older loop.
The cannelés/canelés initial c resembles an opening parenthesis in isolation; it is retained as a letter, not an added delimiter.
The overwrite at certains is visible; the old des reading remains uncertain.
The first P is raised in the gap after stratifications; no separate caret is visible.
The X after modérés is baseline-aligned; H's insertion claim is not supported by the inspected alignment.
The (n+1)- replacement is raised; the separate aux overwrite mentioned in H is not securely distinguishable. No extra deleted aux was invented.
H's top-word note admits reading uncertainty; visible letters permit the topis/topos transcription.
H's explanation of s- is editorial, not a doubt mark; the actual short prefix remains ss-/s-.
The sign before ch. has two components, both preserved; their role remains à/colon uncertain.
The underline exists under Hom only. H's textual omission is reported, and its note's broader RHom wording is not imported.
Quoted English versions and other-page references in supplied comments were not consulted or used as reading evidence.
